DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, EDUCATION, AND WELFARE
OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY
WASHINGTON, D.C. 20201
192.
J. 12. 25 1972
Mr. G. Douglas Hofe, Jr.
Director
Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
U. S. Department of the Interior
Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Mr. Hofe:
This is in response to your letter of June 1, 1972, wherein you requested comments on the draft environmental impact statement for the proposed implementation of Executive Order 11644 which pertains to the use of off-road vehicles on the public lands.
This Department has reviewed the health aspects of the above proposal as presented in the documents submitted. The following comments are offered:
1. The human impacts portion of the text places emphasis on economic factors, aesthetic factors and personal inconvenience for users and non-users of off-road vehicles but gives inadequate attention to potential public health hazards associated with the use of such vehicles. For example, it is not specific as to protective measures that will be needed to prevent pollution of land areas and water supplies by indiscriminate discharge of human body discharges at large organized off-road vehicle events or along trails and in areas where sanitary facilities are widely separated or non-existent.
2. No provision is made in the draft for amending or rescinding area designations (Section 8 of the Executive Order) where such changes are determined to be needed based on information gathered through monitoring the effects of off-road vehicle use on lands under the Department of the Interior control. Consideration should also be given to need for modifying regulations prescribing operating conditions where research and/or monitoring data so indicate.
3. Certain aspects of safety, such as user safety devices and protection of non-users against injuries caused by off-road vehicles, need to be covered specifically in the text.
